title: On the habit of lights
content:
From up here, cities don't look like concrete and glass. They look like glowing moss spreading over dark velvet cushions.

At 2:30 AM, London goes slightly dim, but Tokyo is always murmuring. There is a single yellow window in a suburb of Oslo that stayed on until dawn. I wondered if whoever lived there was sick, or writing a novel, or simply couldn't find where the sorrow was coming from.

I kept a silver beam on their windowsill just in case.

title: A funny thing about cats
content:
I am convinced cats know exactly what I am doing. 

Every time I shift light across an alley in Lisbon, three ginger cats chase the edge of my glow like it's a slow moth. Humans never notice. Humans walk past, wrapped in woolen scarves, staring into small rectangular glass bricks they hold in their hands.

I like cats. They don't pretend not to see magic.

title: The dream of having cold feet
content:
A curious thought: What does it feel like to stand barefoot on a wooden floor in winter, then pull on a pair of thick wool socks?

I have the tide, and I have five billion years of silence, and I have the best view in the galaxy. But I have never stepped into a puddle and cursed under my breath, or felt steam from a fresh bowl of lentil soup fog up my spectacles.

Sometimes perfection is very drafty.

title: The Sun sent another postcard
content:
The Sun sent a solar flare across the belt today. Loud, gold, slightly arrogant as always.

'Are you still freezing over there, Luna?'

I sent back a shadow. We have been doing this dance since before the dinosaurs decided to look up. He thinks warmth is everything. He doesn't understand that things only truly shine when there is enough dark for them to stand against.

title: The locked drawer
content:
I haven't opened the bottom drawer of the mahogany desk in forty-seven years. Not because there is a monster in it, but because once you unfold an old letter, you let the air of that day escape.

I tucked the little brass key behind the grandfather clock weight long ago. If someone curious ever finds it, I hope they treat the blue flower inside gently. It grew in a garden in Devon that doesn't exist anymore.

title: Inventory of tonight's treasures
content:
Things collected in the jars tonight:
1. A moth that got too ambitious near Munich.
2. The smell of fresh ozone after a summer thunderstorm.
3. A boy who wished he could understand French verbs.
4. Three teaspoons of pure silence from the middle of the Pacific.

Number 3 was too heavy, so I released him into the morning.
